properties.areaDesc: Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 8 at 12:26PM AKST until November 10 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between two and eight inches and ice accumulations around a light
glaze. Winds gusting as high as 60 mph, mainly across southern
parts of the Anchorage Hillside.

* WHERE...Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River.

* WHEN...From noon Monday to 3 PM AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Monday evening and Tuesday morning commutes. Strong
winds could cause damage to trees and power lines.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong storm system moving across the Gulf
of Alaska will bring a mix of snow, freezing rain and rain to much
of the Anchorage Hillside and Eagle River between Monday afternoon
and early Tuesday afternoon.  Precipitation will start as mainly
heavy snow by Monday afternoon, then transition to a mix of snow
and freezing rain late Monday night to early Tuesday morning as
east winds begin to pick up. Precipitation could transition to
plain rain by Tuesday morning as temperatures rise above freezing.
Uncertainty for the timing of precipitation type transition remains
high, with a later transition to rain and freezing rain potentially
leading to higher snowfall totals.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

between Monday evening and early Tuesday morning.  A transition to
plain rain is possible by around midday Tuesday as temperatures
warm above freezing.  Uncertainty for the timing of precipitation
type transition remains high, with a later transition to rain and
freezing rain possibly leading to higher snowfall totals.

Saint Croix south to 17N and Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from
10 NM to 17N, including the coastal waters of Saint Croix.

agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 8 at 12:17PM PST until November 9 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves 22 to 24
feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides
will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt
Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between
8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 10 PM PST this evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 10 AM to noon PST Monday.
High tide is at 10:54 AM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide
gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before
and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Dangerous
surf conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is
highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The large surf on Sunday will coincide
with high astronomical tides and high tidal anomalies. This
will allow significant runup onto area beaches and may impact
normally dry land or even roads or parking lots.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.
